title: River Flow Lab: An interactive teaching tool for river hydraulics and design
description:
River Flow Lab is a teaching tool for architecture and urban design students that shows how a river's water level and speed respond to its flow and to what is built in and beside it: obstructions, bridges, flood walls, buildings and floating objects. It runs entirely in the browser and ships as a single self-contained HTML file, with no install.

The water surface is solved for one steady flow by the standard-step method in one dimension, following HEC-RAS's steady-flow method: conveyance subdivision with Manning's equation, contraction and expansion losses, the energy method through a bridge with Yarnell's pier equation alongside, a broad-crested weir over an overtopped deck, and eddy zones sized by expansion and contraction ratios. Every result is read as a change against the same river without the design.

The river can be a template reach, a line drawn on a map or taken from OpenStreetMap, a terrain model, or surveyed sections, and a flow can come from a simple float survey. With the bed's material chosen, it shows where the flow can move the bed, by Shields' threshold. The method notes in docs/method-notes.html document every assumption, name every source the code implements, and declare what the tool does not model. It is a teaching model, not a flood risk assessment.
